subject: Urgent: Elevated 5xx/429 + retry storm impacting Nimbus analytics (Dedicated pool)
messages:
From: Claire Hsu <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nimbus-analytics.com>, Nimbus SRE Team <sre@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 5xx / 429 spikes since 08:55PT — production queries failing

Jonas — we started seeing a major spike in 5xx and 429 responses around 08:55 PT this morning against our dedicated pool. A lot of our batch inference jobs are timing out and our frontend is showing retries that are amplifying the problem.

Quick summary: 
- Elevated 5xx (mainly 503/500) and 429 observed across /v1/generate endpoints
- Error bursts coincide with heavy inference window (short LLM responses, many concurrent sessions)
- Clients report ~30% p95 latency regression and a handful of timeouts 

We attached an error sample and a short latency graph. Can you confirm whether you see autoscaling activity or GPU drain on your side? This is affecting our customers — we need an ETA on mitigation.

Attachments: nimbus_5xx_sample.log (text), svc_latency_graph_0914.png (image)

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Ops, Nimbus Analytics

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Claire Hsu <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, seang@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx / 429 spikes since 08:55PT — production queries failing

Claire — thanks for the signal and the logs. I've opened a PagerDuty incident and looped in Engineering and Capacity. Short answers up front: we are seeing rapid scale activity but also a transient burst of GPU OOM+preemption events in your Dedicated pool which correlates with the 5xx spike. Working the next steps below.

Immediate actions I'm coordinating now: 
- Rishi (infra): validate active scaling events and any throttling/fallbacks in the pool
- Marissa (Customer Success): prepare a customer comms template and offer immediate mitigation (traffic shift to hosted fallback or temporary throughput cap)
- Engineering on-call (Sean): triage root cause — check kube/gpu driver logs and model hotshard KV-cache behavior

Would you be able to accept a temporary traffic shift to a hosted pool for critical routes while we stabilize? That would stop the retry amplification.

Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, seang@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx / 429 spikes since 08:55PT — production queries failing

TL;DR: Confirming autoscaler lag + GPU exhaustion pattern. Details: 

Observed signals (infra):
- Autoscaler started provisioning + attaching nodes at 08:58 PT but several GPU instances failed prewarm (driver crash) during model load, leading to capacity under-reporting in the pool.
- SRE saw repeated pod restarts; kube-scheduler backoff stretched out to minutes, causing shortfalls for burst traffic.
- KV cache thrashing on the largest model increased memory pressure — some worker containers hit GPU OOM and returned 5xx.

Immediate mitigations applied: 
1) Disabled aggressive autoscale policy for the pool (fallback to conservative burst policy)
2) Pinned a compatible driver kernel and forced one-off node recycle to stop prewarm failures
3) Rate-limited new session ramp for Nimbus to 60% of baseline to reduce retry amplification

I'll stay on the call until we confirm metrics look normal. Full logs uploaded to the incident link.

— Rishi (Infra Lead)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Claire Hsu <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, seang@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx / 429 spikes since 08:55PT — production queries failing

Claire — we recommend the following immediate customer-facing steps (we can push these now if you approve):
- Mute client-side auto-retries for 10–20 minutes via a feature-flag (prevents retry storm)
- Shift high-priority routes to our hosted fallback pool (we will throttle to safe throughput)
- We will provide an incident status note you can send to your customers — short, transparent, and with mitigation ETA

If you want us to initiate the hosted shift, give a go-ahead and a list of route IDs. We can backfill tokens and maintain request affinity.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Claire Hsu <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>, Nimbus SRE Team <sre@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx / 429 spikes since 08:55PT — production queries failing

Jonas/Marissa — please proceed with the hosted fallback for critical routes. We'll accept a temporary throughput cap and will mute client retries per Marissa's guidance. Route list attached. Please prioritize preserving session continuity for active customers.

Attachments: route_list_nimbus_critical.txt

Tom
Director, Platform Engineering — Nimbus Analytics

From: seang@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx / 429 spikes since 08:55PT — production queries failing

Update from Eng on-call: 
- Hosted fallback completed for the 6 critical routes at 10:20 PT; latency and error rate for those routes dropped immediately.
- Remaining 5xx spikes are correlated with the remaining Dedicated pool nodes that are still cycling; we forced a targeted node-replacement and applied a driver patch to reduce model load failures.
- Monitoring: p95 latency is returning to baseline but we're seeing a smaller residual 429 cluster from client retries. Recommend continuing the client retry mute for 30m and keep the throughput cap.

I'll follow up with a short postmortem doc once we stabilize.
— Sean Gallagher (Engineering on-call)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Claire Hsu <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, seang@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx / 429 spikes since 08:55PT — production queries failing

Claire/Tom — quick status update and next steps now that we're past the immediate incident window: 
- Status: primary errors cleared, 5xx+429 rates at normal range for all routes; small remaining error trace for a subset of heavy models that we'll address in the postmortem.
- Root cause (preliminary): a combination of GPU driver prewarm failures + autoscaler pacing that created a temporary capacity gap during a high-concurrency burst; KV-cache thrash amplified memory pressure and led to OOMs on a few nodes.
- Short-term remediation: updated autoscale policy, driver patch, temporary traffic shaping, hosted fallback for critical routes.
- Long-term actions:
  * Improve autoscaler warm-up heuristics (reduce reliance on immediate attachment metrics)
  * Add probe-based prewarm validation for nodes before routing live traffic
  * KV-cache resiliency: fallbacks to smaller context sizes under memory pressure
  * Run a focused load test on customer's production-like traffic profile

I'll run a joint postmortem with Nimbus on Friday and share the doc + timeline for permanent fixes. Thanks for your patience and for coordinating the mitigations — appreciate the quick approvals.

Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: nimbus_kvcache_dump.txt
